requiredText: The itinerary, hotels and flights, fellow travelers, contacts, destination guides and daily trivia from your current journey app.

Already settled at Raffles, enjoy Singapore before tonight’s official welcome.
A WELCOME FROM YOUR TOUR DIRECTOR
Kingdoms and Dragons, Singapore to Indonesia

Welcome to Singapore! You have selected an awe-inspiring itinerary! I want to take this opportunity welcome you to Singapore and the Raffles Hotel. I am sure you will find Raffles Hotel a comfortable place to relax after your long journey.

This packet includes general information about the tour along with the itinerary and guest information form. Please read it carefully as it will answer some of your immediate questions. The itinerary is made in advance. Changes can occur. Always expect the unexpected. That brings a sense of adventure.

Kindly read all of the attached information carefully and complete the enclosed questionnaire. By doing so, you will greatly assist me in pre-registering you with your rooms and dietary requests at the various hotels and restaurants as soon as possible. I thank you in advance for filling out this paperwork. Please bring the completed paperwork with you to our welcome reception on Saturday, Day 1, which will be in the East India room at 17:30. Please bring the following;
Guest questionnaire – please answer all the questions!
Choice of your dinner for the Welcome dinner.

For those who have arrived early – please rest. If you want to get out to do some sightseeing, your room butler can also assist with restaurants reservations, transportation and other options for you. Consider your butler as your personal concierge. You may also use my recommendations in this package or reach out to me via WhatsApp if you have any questions or require any assistance. Don’t forget to enjoy your complimentary Singapore Sling, this can be booked through your Butler or at the Concierge desk. You can also skip the line at the Long Bar. There is a pool, gym and spa on property. There is a tour of the Raffles that can be taken each afternoon, we are asked to book in advance!

As your Tour Director, I will accompany you from the beginning of our trip through the end, and will supervise accordingly. I will do everything possible to ensure that our journey runs as smoothly and carefree as possible so that you can absorb and enjoy these remarkable countries. Sit back, relax… Enjoy your vacation. I am here to assist you in any way I can. I look forward to sharing this experience with you.
Meet for the welcome cocktail and tour briefing at the East India Room, by the fountain. Welcome dinner in the hotel follows the reception.
Please bring the completed guest questionnaire, your welcome-dinner choice, and waiver forms to the reception.
Tap any recommendation to open it in Google Maps. Reservations are especially important for Jumbo Seafood, Keng Eng Kee, Kotuwa, Peach Blossoms, Odette, and HolyCrab.
Song Fa Bak kut teh—peppery pork-rib broth with fried dough sticks. ↗
Jumbo Seafood Singapore seafood institution; chili crab with fried mantou buns. ↗
Keng Eng Kee Seafood Family-run zi char; coffee pork ribs, moonlight hor fun, chili crab, and prawn-paste chicken. ↗
Samy’s Curry North and South Indian cooking; fish-head curry and fish-potato croquettes on a banana-leaf set. ↗
Kotuwa Chef Rishi Naleendra’s Sri Lankan cooking; crab curry, egg hoppers, and mutton rolls. ↗
The Coconut Club Modern nasi lemak with fried chicken, sambal, peanuts, anchovies, and coconut rice. ↗
Peach Blossoms Modern Chinese cuisine and Marina Bay views; steamed carrot cake with lobster, drunken-crab noodles, and the Forbidden Roll. ↗
National Kitchen by Violet Oon Peranakan and Singaporean classics in the National Gallery; dry laksa or beef rendang with sambal eggplant and traditional kueh for dessert. ↗
Lau Pa Sat Victorian-style market and evening satay street; try skewers and fresh sugar-cane juice. ↗
Albert Centre Market & Food Centre Local Bugis market for chicken rice, fishball noodles, laksa, and ice kacang. ↗
Market Street Hawker Centre Modern two-level centre at CapitaSpring; Ipoh hor fun, truffle wonton mee, and biryani. ↗
Maxwell Food Centre Famous, easy-to-navigate centre; Tian Tian chicken rice or fish-noodle soup. ↗
Narrative Coffee Stand Local roasters serving cold brew and espresso-style coffee. ↗
Ya Kun Kaya Toast Kaya toast breakfast sets with local kopi. ↗
Toast Box Singaporean coffee and kaya-toast breakfast sets. ↗
My Awesome Cafe Local vegan café with a vibrant interior, popular for after-work drinks. ↗
Birds of Paradise Gelato Boutique Botanical gelato inspired by herbs, flowers, and Southeast Asian flavors. ↗
Chin Chin Eating House Old-school Hainanese comfort food and classic chicken rice. ↗
New Ubin Seafood Singaporean seafood and zi char in a lively communal setting. ↗
Odette Modern French tasting menus with optional wine pairing; reservations required. ↗
HolyCrab Playful Singaporean crab dishes; try pepper crab with crispy mantou. ↗
Nutmeg & Clove Award-winning cocktails inspired by Singapore’s history and flavors. ↗
LeVeL33 Marina Bay views from a high-rise microbrewery. ↗
Caffe Fernet Italian restaurant and bar overlooking Marina Bay. ↗
Rooftop Bar at Heritage Casual rooftop views of Boat Quay and Marina Bay. ↗
Night Hawk Intimate speakeasy with creative menus and cocktails. ↗
Jigger & Pony Acclaimed cocktail bar celebrated for beautifully executed classics. ↗
Bar KAP Teochew-inspired cocktails in a historic mansion setting. ↗
A FEW WORDS GO A LONG WAY
English is widely spoken in Singapore. Malay is one of its official languages; try these friendly phrases with Malay speakers.
Say it using the English sound guide. These are approximate sounds: “ah” as in father, “ee” as in see, “ng” as in sing, and “g” as in go. Keep the syllables gentle and even.
Good morning Selamat pagi Say: suh-lah-maht pah-gee
Good afternoon (around midday) Selamat tengah hari Say: suh-lah-maht tuh-ngah hah-ree
Good afternoon / early evening Selamat petang Say: suh-lah-maht puh-tahng
Good evening / good night Selamat malam Say: suh-lah-maht mah-lahm
Goodbye / see you again Jumpa lagi Say: joom-pah lah-gee
Thank you Terima kasih Say: tuh-ree-mah kah-see
You’re welcome Sama-sama Say: sah-mah sah-mah
Please (when asking for help) Tolong Say: toh-long
Excuse me / I’m sorry Maaf Say: mah-ahf
How are you? Apa khabar? Say: ah-pah kah-bar
Discover colonial grace, river life, and a more personal side of Singapore.
Breakfast available in the Tiffin Room, located in the lobby.

Meet in the lobby and walk together to the coach. Walking tour through Singapore’s colonial district and a bumboat ride on the river. Dress comfortably for hot and humid weather; bring a hat, sunscreen, an umbrella in case of rain, and comfortable walking shoes.
Lunch at the InTan home, surrounded by museum-worthy art, furniture, and memorabilia. Remove shoes before entering; socks are welcome.
Estimated return to the hotel. The remainder of the afternoon and evening is at leisure. Restaurant reservations through the concierge or butler are recommended.
The afternoon and evening are at leisure after the estimated 2:30 PM return.

Breakfast available at the Tiffin Room.
Meet at the East India Room for a lecture on equatorial forests. Be ready to depart directly afterwards for Gardens by the Bay.
Guided visit of the Flower Dome and Cloud Forest. If the Cloud Forest is closed for maintenance, visit the Supertree Observatory instead.
Transfer back to the hotel, remain at Gardens by the Bay for lunch, or choose a drop-off at Marina Bay Sands or the National Gallery.
Meet at the East India Room for the lecture, ready to depart immediately afterwards.

Fly to Java’s artistic heart and retreat to serene Amanjiwo.

Luggage collected outside your room. No power banks in checked luggage. Keep your carry-on with you and bring it to the coach. Regular TSA restrictions apply for the international flight to Indonesia.
Depart for the airport. Check all belongings, empty your safe, settle bills, and return your key; forgotten items are difficult or impossible to send to Indonesia.
Scoot TR248 flight to Yogyakarta, approximately two hours. Java is one hour behind Singapore.
Arrive and board the coach for a 90-minute drive through the Java countryside to Borobudur.
Estimated arrival at Amanjiwo Hotel. Lunch upon arrival.
Complimentary tea at the Terrace Bar.
Indonesian barbecue dinner with entertainment by the hotel pool.
Java is one hour behind Singapore. Keep power banks out of checked luggage.
Arrival in Java, followed by the transfer to Amanjiwo
Java — The Island That Built Indonesia
A six-minute journey through Java’s history, temples and traditions.
A FEW WORDS GO A LONG WAY
Indonesian is used across Java, Bali and Komodo. These phrases work throughout this part of our journey, alongside the local languages.
Say it using the English sound guide. These are approximate sounds: “ah” as in father, “ee” as in see, “ng” as in sing, and “g” as in go. Keep the syllables gentle and even.
Good morning Selamat pagi Say: suh-lah-maht pah-gee
Good day / early afternoon Selamat siang Say: suh-lah-maht see-ahng
Good afternoon (late afternoon) Selamat sore Say: suh-lah-maht soh-reh
Good evening (after dark) Selamat malam Say: suh-lah-maht mah-lahm
Good night (at bedtime) Selamat tidur Say: suh-lah-maht tee-door
Goodbye / see you Sampai jumpa Say: sahm-pie joom-pah
Thank you Terima kasih Say: tuh-ree-mah kah-see
You’re welcome Sama-sama Say: sah-mah sah-mah
Please (when asking for help) Tolong Say: toh-long
Excuse me (getting attention / passing) Permisi Say: puhr-mee-see
How are you? Apa kabar? Say: ah-pah kah-bar
Ma’am / Mrs. / Ms. (respectful address) Ibu Say: ee-boo
Sir / Mr. (respectful address) Bapak Say: bah-pahk

A little local courtesy: Ibu and Bapak literally mean mother and father, but are also respectful ways to address adults. You may hear the shorter forms Bu (“boo”) and Pak (“pahk”). At Amanjiwo, staff use them as a warm sign of respect. Use Selamat malam to greet someone after dark; Selamat tidur wishes someone a good sleep.
Experience Borobudur at sunrise, then explore Candirejo Village before an afternoon at Amanjiwo.
Coffee, tea, juice, and cookies at the Aman bar area.
Arrive at Borobudur; sandals and flashlights will be distributed.
Sunrise tour ends; depart for Aman. Breakfast at Aman on return.
Depart for Candirejo Village for a horse-carriage / walking tour.
Return to Aman. Lunch at your leisure.
Lecture on the Kingdoms of Java in the art room upstairs.
Dinner at your leisure. No reservations needed; choose when and with whom you would like to dine.
The sunrise visit replaces the usual Borobudur program because of closures. Bring your hearing devices and camera, and dress for hot and humid weather.

Enjoy a leisurely morning at Amanjiwo with breakfast and an early lunch at the hotel. Breakfast and lunch can be served by the pool. Enjoy the hotel bikes, pool, surroundings, or watercolor painting.
Luggage collected inside your villa. Settle incidentals, return room keys, and check all your belongings.
Check in at Yogyakarta Marriott Hotel for one night.
Depart for the Prambanan Temple Complex. Walking tour with many uneven steps; bring mosquito repellent for the sunset visit.
Included dinner, followed by the outdoor Javanese Ramayana performance telling the story of King Rama and Sita, with Prambanan Temples in the background.
Show starts. Stay until intermission, then depart for the hotel.
Luggage is collected inside your villa at 11:30 AM. Bring mosquito repellent for the outdoor temple visit.

Breakfast opens in Yogyakarta Kitchen. Allow time for the large buffet.
Depart for Yogyakarta Airport. Do not leave anything behind.
Fly to Bali on IU123, approximately 1 hour 30 minutes. Bali is one hour ahead of Java. The drive to Ubud is approximately 90 minutes, depending on traffic.
Quick stop for toilets, juice, and a small snack.
Visit the iconic Monkey Forest in Ubud.
Dinner is included on one evening of the three-night stay, with reservations taken in advance. Arrange other resort dinners with the concierge. Alcohol is not included.

Depart from the entrance for Melinggih Kelod Village and a walking tour.
Lunch overlooking the rice fields at Begawan Biji Restaurant.
Approximate return to the hotel. Afternoon at leisure: enjoy the spa, massage, plunge pool, town, or a hotel restaurant.
Allow time for the buggy ride to breakfast before the 8:45 AM departure.

Both storage bags and duffel bags are collected. Keep hand luggage with you and bring it to the bus.
Depart for the airport; the drive can take 90 minutes.
Flight departs for Labuan Bajo, Flores. On arrival, transfer to the beachfront resort outside town for lunch and check-in. The remainder of the day is at leisure.
Seafood barbecue dinner with local folk dancing on the beach. Alcohol is not included.
Keep carry-on luggage with you. The flight departs at 11:40 AM.

Return to Plataran Resort, or choose to snorkel in the Flores Sea.
Included dinner at leisure at Atlantis or Xanadu. Alcohol is not included.
Wear closed shoes for the Rinca Island trek. Lunch is at Menjaga Bay Resort.

A WELCOME FROM YOUR TOUR DIRECTOR
Kingdoms and Dragons, Singapore to Indonesia

Welcome to Singapore! You have selected an awe-inspiring itinerary! I want to take this opportunity welcome you to Singapore and the Raffles Hotel. I am sure you will find Raffles Hotel a comfortable place to relax after your long journey.

This packet includes general information about the tour along with the itinerary and guest information form. Please read it carefully as it will answer some of your immediate questions. The itinerary is made in advance. Changes can occur. Always expect the unexpected. That brings a sense of adventure.

Kindly read all of the attached information carefully and complete the enclosed questionnaire. By doing so, you will greatly assist me in pre-registering you with your rooms and dietary requests at the various hotels and restaurants as soon as possible. I thank you in advance for filling out this paperwork. Please bring the completed paperwork with you to our welcome reception on Saturday, Day 1, which will be in the East India room at 17:30. Please bring the following;
Guest questionnaire – please answer all the questions!
Choice of your dinner for the Welcome dinner.

For those who have arrived early – please rest. If you want to get out to do some sightseeing, your room butler can also assist with restaurants reservations, transportation and other options for you. Consider your butler as your personal concierge. You may also use my recommendations in this package or reach out to me via WhatsApp if you have any questions or require any assistance. Don’t forget to enjoy your complimentary Singapore Sling, this can be booked through your Butler or at the Concierge desk. You can also skip the line at the Long Bar. There is a pool, gym and spa on property. There is a tour of the Raffles that can be taken each afternoon, we are asked to book in advance!

As your Tour Director, I will accompany you from the beginning of our trip through the end, and will supervise accordingly. I will do everything possible to ensure that our journey runs as smoothly and carefree as possible so that you can absorb and enjoy these remarkable countries. Sit back, relax… Enjoy your vacation. I am here to assist you in any way I can. I look forward to sharing this experience with you.

The hotel opened in 1887 and became one of Singapore’s great historic landmarks.
The Singapore Sling was created at Raffles’ Long Bar in the early 20th century.
English, Malay, Mandarin Chinese, and Tamil are Singapore’s four official languages.
Cherry liqueur is one of the cocktail’s best-known ingredients.
Warehouses, boats, and merchants made the river the commercial heart of early Singapore.
Bumboats transported cargo between ships and the river’s busy quays.
Katong and nearby Joo Chiat are celebrated for Peranakan culture and ornate shophouses.
The riverside quay was named for Sir Andrew Clarke, Governor of the Straits Settlements.
The Supertrees range up to about 50 meters, or roughly 164 feet.
Cloud Forest’s misty mountain is built around a dramatic indoor waterfall.
Guinness recognized it as the world’s largest glass greenhouse when it opened.
Some Supertrees use photovoltaic cells to harvest solar energy for lighting.
Borobudur rises in Central Java near Yogyakarta.
The vast 8th- and 9th-century complex is one of the world’s greatest Buddhist monuments.
Dozens of perforated stupas surround the great central stupa.
UNESCO inscribed the Borobudur Temple Compounds on its World Heritage List in 1991.
Ascending its terraces symbolically moves from the earthly realm toward enlightenment.
Millions of blocks of dark volcanic andesite stone form the monument.
Active Mount Merapi is a defining feature of Central Java’s landscape.
Central Java’s humid landscape often creates atmospheric morning mist around the monument.
Prambanan’s soaring temples honor the Hindu trinity of Shiva, Vishnu, and Brahma.
The epic follows Rama’s quest to rescue his wife Sita from the demon king Ravana.
Yogyakarta is one of Indonesia’s great centers for handmade batik.
The central Shiva temple is the tallest and largest structure in the Prambanan complex.
The Island of the Gods reflects Bali’s thousands of temples and rich spiritual life.
Hundreds of Balinese long-tailed macaques live in the forest sanctuary.
Balinese Hinduism blends Hindu traditions with local customs and ancestral beliefs.
The name reflects the area’s traditional association with medicinal herbs and healing.
Canang sari are woven palm-leaf trays filled with flowers, incense, and symbolic gifts.
Subak coordinates water, farming, and temple life across Bali’s rice terraces.
A sarong and sash show respect and are commonly required at temple sites.
Rice cultivation has shaped Bali’s landscape, communities, and temple traditions for centuries.
Pandan gives many Southeast Asian sweets their distinctive aroma and green color.
Nasi means cooked rice, as in nasi goreng, Indonesia’s famous fried rice.
Painting, carving, dance, music, and craft traditions flourish throughout Ubud.
Layered bronze gongs and metallophones create gamelan’s distinctive interlocking rhythms.
Labuan Bajo is a harbor town on the western end of Flores.
Portuguese sailors named the island Cabo de Flores, meaning Cape of Flowers.
The park protects islands and marine waters within Indonesia’s Lesser Sunda Islands.
Boats depart Labuan Bajo for the islands and waters of Komodo National Park.
Adult Komodo dragons can grow to about 10 feet and weigh well over 150 pounds.
Their wild range is limited to a few islands in and around Komodo National Park.
Like other monitor lizards, it samples scent particles with its forked tongue.
Its reefs, seagrass beds, and marine life make the park celebrated both above and below water.
Dozens of performers create rhythmic interlocking chants with no traditional gamelan orchestra.
Jimbaran sits on Bali’s southwestern coast facing the Indian Ocean.
Kite flying is woven into village life, seasonal winds, and religious expression.
The chorus repeats rhythmic cak sounds while forming dramatic interlocking patterns.
The temple is perched high above the Indian Ocean on Bali’s southern cliffs.
Garuda is Vishnu’s great eagle-like mount and Indonesia’s national emblem.
Pura is the Balinese word commonly used for a Hindu temple.
Bali’s important sea and directional temples are traditionally understood as spiritual guardians of the island.
Seafood restaurants line the beach, with tables set directly on the sand.
Terima kasih is the standard Indonesian expression of thanks.
Bali sits at the western end of Indonesia’s Lesser Sunda island chain.
Many beachside kitchens use coconut husks to give grilled seafood a smoky aroma.
